name: p3c-prefill-cut-stress
basis: P2C completed with 240 responses/arm: AIME 4k->8k slope +14.6 points; admission-only arrival 41.7% correct-on-time; live 39.2%, fixed8k 37.9%, fixed4k 34.6%. The in-flight 8k->4k cut was 2.5 points below admission-only overall and 9.5 below it in the P2C burst window.

The P2C burst hit a partially empty rig: only about 15-25 requests were running when the burst began, so admission alone could send burst arrivals to 4k and avoid most misses. That is not the case in which an in-flight cut is most likely to be justified.

A cut can only beat admission when the queue is already occupied by requests that admission cannot shorten: a burst that arrives while a full cohort of 8k requests is already running. The cut can free those slots earlier; admission can only change new arrivals.
The current cut target is 4k. A less destructive 6k cut may capture most of the slot-release benefit with a smaller accuracy loss. The extension tests both.

The central hypothesis remains: live should deliver more correct-by-deadline answers than a fixed short budget and admission-only, while keeping eventual accuracy close to full thinking. This extension tests its most favorable natural case, not a post-hoc threshold change.

design.purpose: Test whether an in-flight cut is justified when a burst hits a full 8k cohort, and whether a 6k cut preserves more accuracy than the 4k cut while still recovering timeliness.
design.trace_shape: 32 signal requests at 0-0.62 s fill all 32 slots at 8k; 64 requests arrive at 4/s from 10 s; the remaining requests arrive deterministically every 6 s from 120 s to 1080 s. All requests have the same 240 s deadline.
design.why_this_shape: A full running cohort is the one condition where admission cannot shorten the requests that block the burst. If a cut cannot win here, it is hard to justify over admission on this workload.

endpoints.primary: correct-on-time signal responses across all 180 signal responses per arm
secondary: worker cuts, cut after close, pressure, admission budget split
endpoints.failed_outcomes: Caps, missing outputs, late answers and errors stay in the denominator. Correct-on-time requires a correct normal completion received within 240 s of client submission.

validity_requires: all six arm phases present and injection valid
live4k and live6k each have at least one worker cut
no cut after the close token (strict > cue_start)
live arms show both a 4096 and an 8192 admission
fixed4k, fixed6k and fixed8k have zero cuts
cut_stop_if: no live variant beats arrival on correct-on-time
both live variants are more than 10 points below arrival on eventual accuracy
decision.admission_comparison: Report arrival vs fixed4k, fixed6k and fixed8k on the same trace; this independently checks the P2C admission finding on the prefilled-cohort load.
decision.inconclusive: Valid, but the best live variant is between the stop and GO thresholds; record it and do not spend a confirmatory block without a new pre-declaration.

power.note: This is a screening extension, not a powered P2. At 180 responses/arm the 80% MDE is roughly 12-16 points at ICC 0.2-0.6 and 20% discordance. A GO justifies a larger confirmatory run; a STOP is a strong signal against the cut on this workload.
